messages:
maria: paging on-call, org SirenScale is spiking and customers are reporting slow responses and 429s. getting alerts from infra-dashboard and L7 logs. anyone oncall? 

oncall-bot: INCIDENT TRIGGERED: high 429 rate for org=sirenscale - severity=sev2 - page routed to @aj (oncall - infra-rotations). Incident ID: INC-2026-4271

aj: I got it, joining. what's the immediate customer impact?
sylvia: they're hitting our /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings-heavy endpoints—embeddings in particular are spiking qps per org to ~4k sustained, they normally sit at ~600. Errors are mostly 429 + some 504 tail latency.

maria: confirmed, org quota is 800 qps, they're sending a lot of parallel embed requests from batch workers.

aj: TL;DR: customers downstream experiencing throttles and timeouts. need quick mitigation: temporary org rate bump or selective blocking of the heavy embeddings endpoint. prefer minimal customer impact.

kevin: quick idea — bump org QPS to 1200 for 10m, but also enable per-route shaping to limit concurrent embeddings to 20, keep generate route at current QPS. That reduces risk while we investigate root cause.
jess: +1 on shaping. If we just increase org quota we might hit HW capacity and cause cross-org latency. we should set a hard cap on heavy route.

aj: agree. I'll execute emergency adjust. executing command now: ```/rl adjust --org sirenscale --qps 1200 --duration 10m --reason "inc-2123456789 temporary bump"```
oncall-bot: COMMAND RUN: /rl adjust ... — queued on control-plane.
deploy-bot: ORG QUOTA UPDATE: sirenscale qps set to 1200 until 2026-05-01T12:47:00Z (ephemeral).

samir: i also pushed a traffic-shape rule: ```route: /v1/embeddings-heavy, concurrent_limit: 20, queue_size: 50, fallback: 429``` should be active in 30s.

maria: rule is in. seeing decrease in 429s from internal sim clients.

kevin: real-time metrics: overall token-per-sec unchanged, embeddings latency down 40% on 90th pct. but backend GPU utilization on the regional pool went from 72% -> 88% after bump. watching.
aj: keep an eye — if GPU nodes approach 95% we should roll traffic to quantized embeddings variant or throttle further.

jess: i'll open a canary route to embeddings-quant-q4 for new requests: ```canary create --org sirenscale --route /v1/embeddings-heavy --percent 15 --model embeddings-quant-q4```. Doing now.
oncall-bot: CANARY STARTED: 15% traffic to embeddings-quant-q4 for org=sirenscale.

sylvia: early perf looks OK for quant variant, p95 latency ~+12ms but throughput stays stable. quality checks passing for known seed prompts.

maria: reaching out to CS to notify customer point-of-contact and let them know we're doing temporary quota bump + shaping and monitoring.

cs-rep-bot: ALERT SENT: SirenScale POC notified (email + in-app). Template: "We're seeing elevated traffic and have applied a temporary rate adjustment and route shaping to reduce errors. We'll follow up with timeline and root cause."

aj: ok plan: 1) monitor for 20m, 2) if stable, extend bump window and schedule a postmortem; 3) if GPU util > 94% revert bump and shift more traffic to quant canary.

kevin: i'm running a quick log grep for repeated client replays or cron spikes. command: ```kubectl logs -l svc=sirenscale -n prod | grep -E "batch_worker|bulk_embed|/bulk|parallelize" | head -n 50``` — initial look shows a handful of IPs spiking at near 200 rps each.
samir: added IP-based soft rate-limiting rule for those source IPs: ```ip-shape add --ip 203.0.113.42 --qps 80 --duration 20m```

jess: for audit, document the mitigation in the incident channel and tag for postmortem: cause suspected: misconfigured retry/backoff in customer batch system.

maria: update: after 8m, 429 rate down from 9.4% -> 1.3% for org, customer reports fewer timeouts. can we keep the bump and canary for now?
aj: hold bump and canary; extend QPS to 1500 for 20m to let backlog drain, but only if GPU util <= 90%. i'll run the adjust: ```/rl adjust --org sirenscale --qps 1500 --duration 20m --reason "drain backlog"```
oncall-bot: COMMAND RUN: /rl adjust ... — applied.

kevin: note: region-gpu-pool-3 util now 91%. slipping up. if it hits 95% we'll do a rollback.
sylvia: I'll prepare rollback steps: 1) set org qps back to 800, 2) pause embeddings-heavy route (503 fallback), 3) notify customer.

maria: also adding a temporary per-customer burst allowance flag to avoid other orgs getting collateral impact. done via console toggle.

aj: looks like the spike source identified — a scheduled batch job with broken concurrency controls. Maria, can you ask CS to confirm with SirenScale and request they patch their backoff?
maria: pinged CS lead and included logs/samples. they replied acknowledging and said the release to fix retry logic will be deployed in ~3 hours. asked them to shift batch window and throttle.

samir: metrics 12m in: 429 at 0.6%, embeddings p95 stable, GPU util 89%. canary traffic to quant variant showing 0 quality regressions on our test set.
aj: good. transitioning to monitoring-only. i'll handoff to next oncall in 30m for follow-up. please keep incident channel updated if anything changes.

maria: thanks team. final actions before I unpage: - ensure CS confirms customer's patch schedule (done) - leave shaping/canary in place until customer fixes - schedule post-incident review and include logs, commands, and timeline.

deploy-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied: org-qps=1500 (ephemeral), route-shape /v1/embeddings-heavy concurrent_limit=20, canary embeddings-quant-q4=15%.

oncall-bot: HANDOFF: @aj -> @kevin (oncall - infra-rotations) in 30m.

kevin: i'm taking on the watch. will run periodic checks and escalate if util goes >93%.
jess: i'll draft the postmortem and include recommended platform-level guardrails (auto-detect and auto-shape for sudden per-org surge, safer default per-route concurrency).

maria: incident declared resolved for customer impact; continuing monitoring for 2 hours. closing thread when final metrics look stable. :white_check_mark:
